subject: Aggregation (convolution) of raster cell / polygon information

messages.author: ed8725f963b72c68
messages.subject: Aggregation (convolution) of raster cell / polygon information
parts:
I have a spatial layer that provides estimates of a potential biomass supply. (i.e. for each cell / polygon a probability distribution). I would like to aggregate the information in order to obtain the total (sum) supply of biomass within a study area (i.e. on single probability distribution for the entire area).

Is there a possibility to do something like that with R-INLA?

Or in other words: 
Is there a function in R-INLA for convolute multiple probability distributions?

not in general no. you can compute the properties of a sum or mean of a
set of variables from the inla-output, then use inla.posterior.sample()
